# Instructions

This week, you learned several more functions from the dplyr package (pronounced DEE-ply-er). These functions help you work with the rows and columns in your data set.

You'll use these skills to add a new column showing the daily return of each index and investigate whether the indexes display the same pattern of returns across time.

To learn more about the variables contained in the data set, refer to the data dictionary: https://rstudio.github.io/academy-tidyverse-stock-portfolios/assets/indexes_dictionary.html

Remember that all tidyverse packages have already been installed for you but you will need to *load* the ones you want to use.

## Create and select columns

It is hard to compare performance across indexes by looking at prices. In this milestone, you'll create a new variable that shows the daily return of each index. You'll then recode the index tickers into human readable names and explore the cumulative returns over time.

## Recreation

### Part 1 - Import

Before you begin, you will need to import your data set. Use the code chunk below to read the data from the data file `indexes.csv`, which is stored in the `data/` folder in your working directory. Be sure to save the data to an object named `indexes`.

### Part 2 - Create and recode

Run the code below to see a table.

```{r}
#| label: recreate-this
#| message: false
solution <- readr::read_csv("data/milestone03.csv")
solution
```

Your task is to use what you've learned about the dplyr package to transform `indexes` into this table. You will need to:

1. Create a new column named `return`, which computes returns based on the formula: `1 + ((adjusted - lag(adjusted, order_by = date)) / lag(adjusted, order_by = date))`
2. Replace all `NA` values in `return` with 1 using `if_else()`
3. Use `return` to create a new column named `growth` that stores the cumulative returns (Hint: `cumprod()`)
4. Recode each index ticker as follows using `case_when()`:

    - ^DJI : Dow Jones
    - ^FVX : 5 Year Treasury
    - ^GSPC : S&P 500
    - ^IRX : 13 Week Treasury
    - ^IXIC : NASDAQ
    - ^TNX : 10 Year Treasury

_Hint_: What function, placed before `mutate()`, will calculate these values separately for each index?

Work in the code chunk below. Save the result as `indexes_return`.

```{r}
#| label: recreation-create

```

Run the following code chunk to test whether you have the same answer as the solution:

```{r}
#| label: compare
#| eval: false
waldo::compare(indexes_return, solution, tolerance = 1e-4)
```

### Part 3 - Visualize

Now that you have created the `growth` variable, you can plot the cumulative returns growth of each index over time. Run the chunk below to visualize `indexes_return`.

```{r}
#| label: visualize-growth
#| eval: false
indexes_return |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = date, y = growth, color = symbol)) +
    geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Cumulative returns growth of indexes over time")
```
